component_insights.complexity: Improving. Score rose from 88 (Apr 22) to 92 (May 2) to 91 (May 13), net +3 over the window. The refactor that split useCoachThread into focused hooks (PR #100) and the decomposition of db.ts into domain modules (PR #98) drove measurable complexity reduction in the largest files. Current avg cyclomatic of 4.2 across 209 files is healthy. No single file is a dominant outlier — complexity is distributed across page-level aggregators (sleep/page.tsx, recovery/page.tsx) that are expected to have higher fan-out.
component_insights.duplication: Declining. Score fell from 96 (Apr 22) to 88 (May 2) to 91 (May 13), net -5 over the window with the worst point at May 2. The May 2 dip aligns with the coaching and streaming PRs (#105, coach progress streaming) adding new patterns before they were consolidated. The partial recovery to 91 by May 13 reflects some normalisation. At 4.3% duplication (77 clones) this is still within acceptable range but trending wrong. The chart/card components are the likely duplication source — many follow an identical data-fetch + render pattern.
component_insights.coupling: Sharply declining — the worst-performing component. Score dropped from 100 (Apr 22) to 93 (May 2) to 81.3 (May 13), a 19-point fall with a slope of -9.5 and near-perfect correlation (0.99). Two hub-like dependencies are driving this: streamlit/whoop/db.py (fan-in 60, well above the 20 threshold) and apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts (fan-in 31). The auth.ts hub grew rapidly as Phases B–E added Apple Sign-In, multi-user data isolation, onboarding, and the welcome wizard — each new route imported auth.ts. The streamlit/db.py hub is a legacy artifact from the pre-Next.js era; the Streamlit surface is retired but the file still counts in the graph. No cycles exist (0 cyclic count), which is the one positive. Action needed: auth.ts should be split into auth/session, auth/guard, and auth/identity modules. db.py impact should be filtered or weighted down once Streamlit retirement is formalized.
component_insights.cohesion: Strongly improving. Score rose from 93 (Apr 22) to 92 (May 2) to 100 (May 13), a +7 net gain with slope +3.5. The domain module decomposition (db.ts split into recovery, sleep, strain, workouts, integrations, etc.) directly improved cohesion by giving each class a single clear responsibility. Only 1 low-cohesion violation remains: ToolInputError in apps/web/src/lib/coach/tools.ts has LCOM 2 (threshold 1), a minor issue from the class holding a details field alongside constructor logic. All other 15 analyzed classes are clean.
component_insights.smells: Slightly declining but stable. Score fell from 100 (Apr 22) to 94 (May 2) to 95.3 (May 13). The only active smells are the two HubLikeDependency findings (streamlit/whoop/db.py and apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts) — no critical issues, no cycles, no unstable components. The May 2 dip to 94 coincided with the auth hub growing as Apple Sign-In and the Phase C/D multi-user work landed. Score is effectively bounded by whether those two hubs are addressed.
component_insights.satd: Stable and healthy. Score held at 100 across all three snapshots (slope 0.0, correlation 0.0 — no trend). 18 debt items exist with 8 high-priority, but none have crossed the threshold to affect the score. SATD is not a current concern.
component_insights.tdg: Slightly improving. Score rose from 92 (Apr 22) to 93 (May 2) to 93 (May 13), slope +0.5 with strong correlation (0.87). Current avg grade is AMinus across all 209 files. This is consistent with the complexity improvements — the same refactors that reduced cyclomatic complexity also lifted TDG grades. No action needed.
